author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if one simple decision could open the door to possibilities you never imagined?

In this talk, Nduati (Robert) Karanja explores the power of saying yes to opportunities, embracing uncertainty, and stepping beyond the boundaries of what feels familiar. Through his perspective and experiences, he invites us to reconsider how a single choice can shape our journeys, transform our outlook, and create room for unexpected possibilities.

Sometimes, the turning point begins with two simple words: Yes, I will. Robert) Karanja is a financial educator, advisor, entrepreneur, and public speaker with more than 14 years of experience in the financial sector. He is the founder of Cents Sensei and Affluent Financial Consultants, where he promotes financial literacy, investment education, and informed financial decision-making through speaking, training, and digital storytelling. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community.
title: What if you said yes? | Nduati (Robert) Karanja | TEDxArada Live

author: TEDx Talks
description: Based on the campus bakery phenomenon, this speech interprets human behavioural patterns from the perspective of behavioural economics and the concept of choice architecture. It illustrates how environment, conformity and repetition shape seemingly personal preferences. It encourages reflective pause before automatic responses so as to restore individual agency in decision making. Chenrui Zhang is a Senior 1 student at Jinling High School who became fascinated with a simple question: why does everyone line up for the same campus bakery? Her curiosity led her into the world of behavioural economics and choice architecture, where she found that environment, conformity, and repetition quietly shape what we call "personal preference." In her talk, she encourages everyone to pause before their next automatic choice — and take back their agency. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted
title: The Bread Was Never About Bread | Chenrui Zhang | TEDxJLHS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Centered on gender related stereotypes, this speech traces the historical origin of gender norms and cites relevant research evidence. It advocates treating gender norms as reflective reference frameworks rather than behavioural constraints. It puts forward proposals for individuals, education sectors and media to foster an inclusive society free from rigid gender prejudice. Yifan Cao is a Senior 1 student at Jinling High School with a keen eye for the invisible rules that shape how people are "supposed" to behave. Curious about where gender norms come from, she traced their history and dug into the research — and came to believe these norms should be mirrors for reflection, not cages for behaviour. In her talk, she calls on individuals, educators, and the media to help build a world free of rigid prejudice. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Make Us the Owner of Gender Norms | Yifan Cao | TEDxJLHS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: As technology becomes better at performing technical tasks, human skills are becoming more valuable, not less. AI isn't replacing humanity. It's revealing which human abilities matter most. Tim David was once an international award-winning mentalist. He's since written several books on advanced communication strategies, including the Blinkist Top 10 Psychology Book of the Year, "Magic Words." He's traveled to 48 states and multiple countries around the world as a keynote speaker sharing his inspiring message about the magic of human connection at work and in life. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The future belongs to the most human | Tim David | TEDxWatkins Glen

author: TEDx Talks
description: A advogada Ianca Larissa Alves Rosa aborda em sua palestra o enfrentamento à violência doméstica e ao feminicídio a partir de sua história pessoal de superação após o assassinato de sua mãe. No contexto atual, marcado por alarmantes índices de crimes contra a mulher e pela perpetuação do controle coercitivo e do silêncio social, o relato denuncia a urgência do acolhimento e da denúncia precoce. Dessa forma, o tema redefine o conceito de legado: em vez de transmitir um pacto de omissão, medo e dor para as próximas gerações, convoca a sociedade a construir uma herança coletiva fundamentada na coragem, na proteção ativa e na garantia de que nenhuma mulher precise arriscar a vida para conquistar sua liberdade. Ianca Alves é advogada criminalista com atuação em violência doméstica e crimes sexuais, dedicada à defesa dos direitos fundamentais. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.c
title: Sobrevivi ao Feminicídio da Minha Mãe  | Ianca Alves | TEDxSete Lagoas

author: TEDx Talks
description: This speech re-evaluates the conventional notion that travel is the primary approach to broadening horizons. It points out the limitations of knowledge acquired through travelling, and maintains that in depth daily observation paired with critical reflection yields more practical insight. It recommends active curiosity and interpersonal dialogue to gain wisdom from ordinary real life contexts. Shiman Fang is a Senior 1 student at Jinling High School who loves to observe — the people around her, the small moments of daily life, the questions hidden in the ordinary. While many assume travel is the best way to broaden one's horizons, she believes that curiosity and reflection at home can take us even further. In her talk, she rethinks the meaning of "seeing the world" and invites the audience to find wisdom in everyday life. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Is Traveling the Best Way to Broaden Our Horizons? | Shiman Fang | TEDxJLHS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Taking Winston Churchill’s lifelong struggle with depression (the “black dog”) as a case, this speech addresses adolescent mental distress. It presents relevant statistical data on youth mental health, underscoring that mental disorders carry no stigma and professional support should be sought when needed. It highlights persistence and resolution as core strengths for overcoming internal adversity. Chen Ji is a Senior 1 student at Jinling High School who cares deeply about mental health. Inspired by Winston Churchill's lifelong battle with his "black dog" of depression, he wants his peers to know that struggling in the dark is not a weakness — and that seeking help is a kind of strength. In his talk, he shares stories and statistics to remind everyone that persistence through hesitation can lead us out of the darkness. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Honor the Hesitation in the Darkness | Chen Ji | TEDxJLHS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Against the backdrop of advancing artificial intelligence, this speech discusses human uniqueness amid the failure of traditional CAPTCHA verification. Taking Turkish abrash handicraft as an example, it identifies imperfection and emphasis on experiential process as core human attributes. It holds that real world experiences and inherent flaws constitute humanity’s distinctive marks. Tianyi is a Senior 1 student at Jinling High School who keeps up with every leap in artificial intelligence — and keeps asking what makes us human in the first place. When CAPTCHAs began failing to tell people from machines, he found his answer in the imperfect patterns of Turkish abrash handicraft: our flaws, and the experiences that shape us, are exactly what no AI can copy. In his talk, he celebrates the beauty of being wonderfully, imperfectly human. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/t
title: How to Prove You Are a Human? | Yi Tian | TEDxJLHS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: This speech investigates self-consumption triggered by unknown others’ inner mental states. Drawing on psychological theories and personal anecdotes, it demonstrates that people often assume worst-case scenarios under information deficiency. It proposes establishing interpersonal trust and conducting direct communication to mitigate irrational anxiety generated by speculative imagination. Gengyuan Ye is a Senior 2 student at Jinling High School who once spent countless nights imagining the worst about what others thought of him — and then decided to find out why. Drawing on psychological theories and his own anecdotes, he discovered how easily speculation fills the gaps when information is missing. In his talk, he shares how trust and direct communication can quiet the noise inside our heads. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: It's Just Patrick! | Gengyuan Ye | TEDxJLHS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Perché scegliamo la musica che ci accompagna ovunque? Francesco Sbraccia esplora il paesaggio sonoro dell’Homo digitalis, tra playlist personalizzate, rifugi emotivi e cuffie che diventano scudi contro il rumore del mondo. Ma quando la musica ci protegge, rischiamo anche di smettere di ascoltare ciò che ci circonda. Un viaggio tra tecnologia, identità e ascolto, alla riscoperta di una possibilità: trasformare le nostre melodie interiori da barriere a ponti, per ritrovare una sintonia con il mondo e con gli altri. FRANCESCO SBRACCIA - Compositore, pianista, cantautore e docente, affianca alla produzione musicale la ricerca sulla percezione acustica e sull’ecologia dell’ascolto.
Ha composto musiche per il teatro e per formazioni sinfoniche e cameristiche, ha insegnato all’Università di Teramo ed è stato vincitore di Musicultura. Ha inoltre curato la direzione artistica dell’album Pigri, entrato nella cinquina del Premio Tenco 2026, e si dedica alla valorizzazione della musica popolare a
title: Sintonizzati altrove | Francesco Sbraccia | TEDxToranoNuovo

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens when a society loses its connection to art, culture, and empathy?

 In this powerful and thought provoking talk, legendary classical dancer and activist Sheema Kermani dissects the elements of a "dead society", one devoid of creative expression, equality, and social justice.

Drawing on decades of experience at the intersection of performing arts and human rights, she reveals how dance and theatre serve as vital lifeblood to awaken marginalized communities, challenge the status quo and breathe life back into a fractured world. This talk explores the critical space between silence and expression, proving that art is not just entertainment, but a necessary tool for survival and societal transformation.

This talk was given at TEDxDUHS, an independently organized TEDx event exploring the theme "The In Between". Sheema Kermani is a legendary Pakistani classical dancer, choreographer, and a prominent women's rights activist. She is the founder of Tehrik-e-Niswan (The Women's M
title: The importance of art for a thriving society | Sheema Kermani | TEDxDUHS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
How do you rebuild your sense of self when life strips away everything you thought you knew? 

For Rabika Tahir, a resilient blood cancer survivor, the journey back to health wasn't just about medicine, it was about facing the mirror and rediscovering her identity through the transformative power of art and self expression.

In this deeply moving talk, Rabika explores the intersection of severe personal health challenges and creative passion, revealing how the simple act of content creation became a profound tool for mental recovery and reclaiming her narrative.

This talk was given at TEDxDUHS, an independently organized TEDx event exploring the theme "The In Between".   Rabika Tahir represents the brilliance of our own DUHS student body as a Biotechnology student. She is a resilient blood cancer survivor who has navigated profound personal health challenges while maintaining her creative passions and academic trajectory, rabika is also an emerging content creator and makeup artist.
title: Brushing the strokes of recovery: What my mirror taught me | Rabika Tahir | TEDxDUHS

author: TEDx Talks
description: This speech examines the “contextual unseen” concealed by visual imagery. Through analyzing Kevin Carter’s controversial press photograph and the online tragedy of the pink-haired girl, it critiques hasty public judgement based on partial information. It advocates individual rational thinking, empathetic awareness, and enhanced media visual ethics to explore underlying structural causes behind social suffering. Chunkai Yang is a Senior 1 student at Jinling High School who likes to pause and look twice at the images flooding his screen. He believes that behind every striking photograph lies a story the frame cannot hold — a belief shaped by reflecting on Kevin Carter's controversial press photo and the online tragedy of the pink-haired girl. In his talk, he invites the audience to judge less hastily, think more independently, and see beyond the frame. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at http
title: Beyond the Frame — The "Unseen" Kills | Chunkai Yang | TEDxJLHS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Yasser Al-Hozaimi explores the role of meaning in strengthening our values and identity, guiding our choices, and bringing clarity and steadiness to how we understand ourselves and our path in life. Yasser Al-Hozaimi is a content creator interested in making knowledge accessible and sharing values. His talk explores how a sense of meaning strengthens identity, guides choices and brings clarity to the way we understand ourselves and our lives. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Joy of a Meaningful Life | Yasser Al-Hozaimi | TEDxAl Raed

author: TEDx Talks
description: Soad opens up about her grief and how it changed her perspective. Her journey took her from sadness to emotional leadership and to volunteering around the world, showing how loss can become a source of compassion and purpose Soad Lotfy is the Emotional and Behavioral Lead at BISM, with over six years of experience walking alongside children as they grow socially, emotionally, and behaviorally. She holds a Master of Science in Psychology and is deeply drawn to Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) as a way of helping individuals live with meaning and resilience. Her work is centered on empowering children, families, and educators through compassionate, practical psychological tools that foster growth and wellbeing. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Know Thyself | Soad Lotfy | TEDxBISM Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if you didn't have to feel ready, have everything figured out or know exactly where life was taking you to make a difference?

In this inspiring talk, Drishmeet Singh Buttar shares his journey from being suspended from school and losing confidence in himself to topping his class.

Just when he thought his future was set, an unexpected responsibility changed his direction. 

His biggest lesson? You don't need a perfect background to begin. Capability comes through learning, confidence comes through action, and experience comes with time.

Perhaps the question isn't whether you're ready. It's what is still possible. Drishmeet Singh Buttar is the Managing Partner of Healing Super Speciality Hospital, Chandigarh's largest NABH-accredited private healthcare institution. A graduate of the prestigious Army Institute of Law, he combines legal acumen with entrepreneurial vision to emerge as one of the region’s youngest and most impactful healthcare leaders. His research papers have been p
title: Why Failure Should Never Be the End of Your Story | Drishmeet Singh Buttar | TEDxSukhna Lake

deeply about how work and lifeing shape identity, confidence and community and

In her mid-30s, she co-founded a multi-million-pound interim start-up in the Forest of Dean, shifting age-based assumptions. Since then, she has worked across marketing, talent strategy and workforce design, helping organisations unlock overlooked talent through flexible models such as micro-workshops, job-share and fractional roles.

title: Later Greater Lifeing: The Diamond Decade (with BSL) | Sarah Taylor Phillips | TEDxEastgate Street

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We live in an era of unprecedented digital reach, yet true human connection requires deliberate intentionality. Grounded in the perspective of optimistic realism, this talk explores how we can navigate high-velocity, tech-enabled environments without losing depth or agency. Rather than rejecting modern tools, Pren-Tsilya introduces a practical framework designed to elevate focus, build trust, and cultivate authentic presence in our daily lives. By making small, compounding daily shifts, we can harness technology to actively design the meaningful, high-trust relationships that drive real human progress.
 Pren-Tsilya Boa-Guehe is an AI thought leader, author, and former diplomat with two decades of experience in tech, policy, and international affairs. Currently leading Pan-African policy at Google, she previously served as a U.S. Foreign Service Officer driving foreign policies across Africa. An advocate for inclusive growth, Pren-Tsilya speaks on leveraging intentional systems, human
title: Finding love in the age of AI | Pren-Tsilya Boa-Guehe | TEDxNairobi

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Why does the creative economy pay so erratically? Why do viral storytellers stay broke? The industry has never been able to price its real asset, so it prices proxies instead: reach, impressions, followers. My argument is that AI is forcing a correction. As machines flood the world with stories nobody lived, and very few love, authenticity becomes scarce, measurable and priceable. Africa holds the largest reserve of unscraped stories on earth, along with the oldest memory of the storyteller's worth. The Authenticity Premium is Africa's oldest pricing model, where storytellers always had value, and authenticity always commanded a premium.
 Cedric Nzomo has spent almost 20 years in the creative economy, working with hundreds of storytellers across a dozen African countries. His work rests on a simple conviction: everyone has a story that holds value, yet today's most valuable storytellers remain underpaid because nothing in the market measures the value they actually bring. He builds th
title: The Authenticity Premium | Cedric Nzomo | TEDxNairobi

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Challenging what we think selfishness means and why putting yourself first can benefit everyone. Gloucester-born Tyler, inspired by his uncles, transitioned from B-boying to diverse styles like Popping. After graduating from YDA Urban in Swindon, he earned a BPA (Hons) in contemporary dance from the Northern School for Contemporary Dance in 2017. Tyler, a seasoned performer with credits including Breakin' Convention's "Back to the Lab" and venues like the O2 Arena, has graced stages across England. Tyler founded Your Next Move in 2015, transforming youth aspirations in Gloucester through Hip Hop.

Tyler Attwood presents TED TALK:  Why We Need to Rethink Selfishness — challenging what we think selfishness means and why putting yourself first can benefit everyone. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why We Need to Rethink Selfishness (with BSL) | Tyler Attwood | TEDxEastgate Street

description: Live Life with Joy: We live in an age that glorifies constant achievement, urging us to become more, do more, and prove more.  But what if fulfillment begins not with endless striving, but with learning to be fully present in an ordinary life?  This talk explores how contentment, authenticity, and quiet purpose emerge when we stop measuring our worth by what we accomplish and start embracing the simple act of being. Joy Barcoma is a Filipino TV host, comedienne, content creator, pageant queen, and advocate committed to using media as a force for education and social impact. Recognized for connecting with audiences through humor, authenticity, and thoughtful storytelling, she has built a platform that goes beyond entertainment. title: Live Life with Joy! | Joy Barcoma | TEDxManila

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, Director JP Habac reflects on what it means for queer filmmakers to reclaim familiar stories, and why authorship matters just as much as representation. Through stories from his own work, he explores how the perspective behind the camera shapes the way we experience love, loss, and belonging—and how making space for different storytellers ultimately expands the way we see one another. JP Habac obtained his bachelor’s degree in Film from the University of the Philippines and has participated in film labs and workshops such as Asian Film Academy, Generation Campus – Moscow, Southeast Asian Film Lab, and Tribeca Film Institute. His body of work includes the film I’m Drunk, I Love You and LGBTQIA+-themed series such as Gaya sa Pelikula and Drag You & Me, with projects recognized in international festivals including Cairo, Busan, and Shanghai. His most recent film, Olsen’s Day, won Special Citation, Best Actor, Best Cinematography, and Best Director at the CinePanalo Film Fes
title: Same Script. Different Story. | JP Habac | TEDxManila

author: TEDx Talks
description: We spend so much time waiting for the perfect moment to be happy that we forget to enjoy the one we're in. This talk explores how gratitude and living in the present can help teens find more joy, resilience, and meaning every day. From an early age, Saraí has embraced service, gratitude, and curiosity as guiding values in her life. These principles inspire her to support her family and friends. At school, her love of learning motivates her to explore new ideas and contribute to a collaborative environment where curiosity is celebrated. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How to Enjoy the Gift of Life: Being grateful and aware of life | Saraí Cadona | TEDxIGA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Since pageantry’s inception in the Philippines nearly 120 years ago with the advent of the Manila Carnival Queen Competition, pageants have captured a special place in our nation’s public consciousness. From barangay pageants for transgender queens, to pageants for OFWs held on their only days off, to international triumphs like Pia Wurtzbach and Catriona Gray clinching the Miss Universe crown in 2015 and 2018, respectively, pageants have become both a full-fledged industry and a point of national pride. This talk will combine my firsthand experiences as the reigning Miss Universe Philippines with my anthropological and historical research to track the rise of the pageant industrial complex and its role in nation-building and defining the country to international audiences.
 Bea Millan-Windorski is a writer, model, and activist based in Makati and San Juan, La Union. She graduated from the University of Wisconsin-Madison with comprehensive honors and degrees in History, International
title: The role of pageantry in nation-building | Bea Millan-Windorski | TEDxManila

author: TEDx Talks
description: After a series of devastating health crises left Kimberly immobile and fighting for her life, a simple, discarded painted rock found in a park became the catalyst for her emotional recovery. Her TED Talk explores how small, tangible acts of kindness can serve as vital anchors during our darkest moments. By sharing the "Painted Rock" movement, she hopes to inspire the audience to find purpose in their own adversity and understand that hope does not require grandeur, it only requires a willing heart to share light with others.
